email_subject: Application - UX Design Certification Officer, Member Apps
email_body:
Dear EPI team,

I'm applying for the UX Design Certification Officer role for Member Apps.

My work sits where web, design and implementation meet: I build and maintain websites end to end, developed front-end features for a healthcare web application, and now work with external clients across several parallel projects at once. That means reading designs and user flows critically, giving feedback specific enough to act on, and following up until something is actually resolved.

I work remotely with Belgian, Dutch and Turkish clients and colleagues, and I'm fluent in English. Figma, Miro, Jira and Confluence would be new tools for me, but I use comparable ones daily and learn them quickly.

I'd like to explain how I could support your member banks. Would a short call work?

cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at EPI,

Wero's premise — that paying and getting paid in Europe shouldn't need extra apps, extra accounts or guesswork — is the kind of problem I want to work on. It's also why this role appeals to me: the job isn't drawing screens all day, it's making sure many different banks deliver the same clear, trustworthy experience. That balance between a central standard and local implementation is where I've spent most of my working life.

My background combines front-end development and web design with client-facing delivery. I developed and optimised front-end features for a healthcare web application at ViviDoctor, and I've since designed and built websites end to end — structure, layout, accessible markup, content — for clients in Belgium and Türkiye. Today I work with external clients on several parallel projects: consultancy sites, e-commerce stores, and a pharmacists' association where I maintain a consistent layout across roughly 600 member profile pages. That means reading a flow critically, writing feedback specific enough to act on, and following up until it's resolved and re-checked.

Two things in the posting match how I work. First, structure: freelancing and agency work have taught me to keep a clear view of many workstreams at once — different clients, platforms and deadlines — and I'd bring that discipline to tracking member banks across features and countries. Second, communication: I explain technical and design constraints to non-design stakeholders in plain language, and I work in fluent English, with Dutch and Turkish alongside.

I also work from data — GA4, Search Console, Semrush — to find what isn't working and iterate on it, a habit I'd apply to usability tests and post-launch feedback from members. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can help your member banks ship consistently good Wero experiences.

cv_highlights:
- Client-facing web and design delivery across parallel projects: WordPress/Elementor builds for a consultancy, e-commerce stores, and a pharmacists' association with a consistent layout for ~600 member profile pages — consistency at scale.
- Front-end development background (ViviDoctor healthcare app, AngularJS/JavaScript) plus hand-coded work with accessible markup: practical understanding of how UI and user flows are built and where they break.
- Structured multi-workstream follow-up as a freelancer and at Episto and KXP: several client sites, catalogues and content pipelines tracked simultaneously across Belgium and Türkiye.
- Clear communication for non-design stakeholders: technical SEO/GEO audits, documented findings and recommendations, reporting on performance; English fluent, Turkish native, Dutch B1 written.
- Remote-first, multicultural collaboration with external clients and teams, using analytics and reporting tools (Google Analytics GA4, Search Console, Semrush, Ahrefs) to drive iterative improvements.
